identity.name: Care Circle
identity.one_liner: One shared record for a family coordinating the care of a relative.

problem: Families coordinating care for a relative keep the plan in group chats, paper notes and each person's memory. Nobody is sure they are acting on the latest version, and a missed medication change is found out after the fact.

audience.name: Coordinating relative
audience.who: An adult child organising care from another city
audience.need: One record every family member and caregiver sees, so nobody acts on a stale copy

audience.name: Paid caregiver
audience.who: A home-care worker visiting several times a week
audience.need: Today's instructions and medication list without calling the family

goals: A family can run a relative's care from one shared record
A change made by one member is visible to every other member immediately
non_goals: Clinical decision support or medical advice

items.name: Technical implementation
items.statement: Access control is enforced in the database, and a member of one care circle cannot read another circle's record through any route.

items.name: Design
items.statement: A first-time caregiver finds today's medication list in under thirty seconds on a phone.

items.name: Impact
items.statement: A medication change entered by one member appears for every other member without a refresh.

items.name: Originality
items.statement: The shared record answers questions about the care plan from the record itself, with the same access rules as the record.

required.name: AWS Database
required.reason: The organisation's data already lives on AWS and must stay in one account.

required.name: Vercel or v0.app deployment
required.reason: The team's existing deployment pipeline and preview workflow run on Vercel.

preferred.name: v0
preferred.reason: Fastest route to a first interface; not required.

constraints.hosting: Vercel for the front end, AWS for data
compliance: Health-related personal data: access is logged and limited to circle members
